lessons.title: Days of the week
lessons.goal: Name the days and say what day it is.

tip.title: lundi = on Monday
tip.body: Days are masculine and written with a small letter. You don't need a word for "on": lundi = on Monday. Add le for a habit: le lundi = on Mondays (every Monday). To ask the day, French people usually say On est quel jour ? Pronunciation: the -di of lundi, mardi etc. is short and clear; in dimanche the first syllable is said like "dee".

phrases.note: In Québec you'll often hear la fin de semaine.

tip.title: Il est trois heures et quart
tip.body: Always say heure(s): il est une heure, il est trois heures. Quarter past = et quart, half past = et demie, quarter to = moins le quart: il est cinq heures moins le quart = 4:45. Noon is midi, midnight is minuit (no heures). Listen for liaison: deux_heures [dø-zœʁ], trois_heures, six_heures [si-zœʁ], dix_heures, and neuf heures becomes [nœ-vœʁ].

lessons.title: Dates & months
lessons.goal: Say the date, your birthday and when you are free.

tip.title: le premier mai, le deux mai…
tip.body: Dates use le + number + month: le deux mai, le quatorze juillet. Only the first of the month is different: le premier mai. Months are masculine and written with a small letter: janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre. août is said [u] or [ut] — both are heard. To ask the date: On est le combien aujourd'hui ?

lessons.title: à + time, en + month
lessons.goal: Say when something happens: at what time, on which day, in which month.

tip.title: à huit heures, en mai, lundi
tip.body: Time of day: à + time — à huit heures, à midi, à vingt heures trente. Ask with À quelle heure ? From… to… = de… à…: de neuf heures à dix-sept heures. Around = vers: vers midi. Months: en mai, en août, or au mois de mai (both mean "in May"). Days need no word at all: lundi, je travaille. Timetables, shops and appointments use the 24-hour clock: dix-huit heures trente (18:30) — with the 24-hour clock you say the minutes as a number (quinze, trente, quarante-cinq), not et quart or et demie.

culture.title: Meal times, the 24-hour clock & holidays
culture.body: In France lunch is usually eaten between about noon and 2 pm, and dinner is fairly late, often around 8 pm; in smaller towns some shops close over lunch. Timetables, shop hours, appointments and TV listings use the 24-hour clock, and people often say it aloud too: Rendez-vous à quatorze heures. Public holidays in France include le premier mai (Labour Day, when lily of the valley is sold in the street), le quatorze juillet (national day), le quinze août and le onze novembre. When a holiday falls on a Thursday, many people take Friday off too: on fait le pont. Elsewhere: Belgium's national day is le vingt et un juillet, Switzerland's le premier août and Québec's Fête nationale le vingt-quatre juin.
